validity.recommendation: Correct StartState/Province from 'Virginia' to 'West Virginia'. The Phase I distribution trunk line begins at a new interconnection in Morgan County, WV (near Berkeley Springs) and ends at the north end of Mountaineer Gas's Martinsburg-area distribution system in Berkeley County, WV. Both ends are in West Virginia; neither is in Virginia. StartLocation='Berkley' likely intends 'Berkeley [Springs]' (the Morgan County seat) but the state cell is simply wrong, the same find-and-replace/state-mixup pattern flagged elsewhere in this batch (cf. P0176's 'New United Kingdom').
validity.researcher_notes: Existence and the rest of the row are solidly confirmed (see the 'confirmed (caveat)' record below), but the Location cluster's StartState/Province is wrong. Independent primary sourcing: (1) Natural Gas Intelligence, 'Mountaineer Planning $45M Expansion in West Virginia's Eastern Panhandle' (2016-04-04), reporting directly from the PSC filing (Case No. 15-1256): 'The first calls for building a 27.5-mile distribution trunk line, beginning at a new interconnection in Morgan County, WV, with a new transmission line from Columbia Gas Transmission LLC (CGT) and extending to the northern end of the company's distribution system, which serves the area of Martinsburg, WV.' (2) West Virginia Public Broadcasting, 'Regulators to Hear Mountaineer Gas Pipeline Expansion Plan': describes the same Segment 1 as running between Berkeley Springs and 'just north of Martinsburg,' both in WV, and names the counties as Morgan, Jefferson and Berkeley -- all West Virginia counties. (3) WVDEP news release on the construction stormwater permit: route is in 'Morgan and Berkeley Counties, West Virginia.' (4) Mountaineer Gas's own site (mountaineergasonline.com/news.html): 'Expand service into Morgan (unserved)...and eventually Jefferson Counties (unserved)' -- again West Virginia counties. No source places any part of Phase I in the Commonwealth of Virginia. Only StartState/Province is disputed; StartLocation, EndLocation ('Martinsburg'), EndState/Province ('West Virginia'), and StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea ('United States') are consistent with all sources and not contested, so I have not staged a fills[] entry for the Location cluster (doing so would pair a ref against the still-wrong Virginia value). LengthKnown (44.30 km = 27.5 mi) matches the PSC-filed Phase 1 mileage almost exactly, which independently confirms this is the same segment being discussed.

validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and well documented, independent of GEM/gem.wiki and independent of abarrelfull/theodora (neither appears anywhere in this trail). This is Segment 1 ('Phase I') of Mountaineer Gas Company's PSC-approved Eastern Panhandle Market Expansion (EPME), West Virginia PSC Case No. 15-1256-G-390P, filed ~2016-03-31 (Natural Gas Intelligence, 2016-04-04, reporting directly from the filing) and covered independently by WV Public Broadcasting (PSC hearing, Oct 2016), the West Virginia Press Association/State Journal (2017-03-06, VP Moses Skaff interview), the WV Dept. of Environmental Protection (construction stormwater permit news release, ~Feb 2018), Marcellus Drilling News (2018-06, summarizing WVDEP approval + construction start), the Herald-Mail/Hagerstown (2019-01-03, 'first segment...nearly complete'), and Mountaineer Gas's own site (mountaineergasonline.com/news.html, 'Eastern Panhandle Pipeline Project'). CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas pipeline; it is an intrastate LOCAL-DISTRIBUTION trunk line (Mountaineer Gas Company is a WV LDC, PSC-regulated, not FERC), matching the scope brief's own framing -- not a misclassification. DUPLICATE: NOT a duplicate of P2040 -- P2040 is EPME Segment 2 ('Charles Town Loop', ~24.5 mi, Martinsburg->Charles Town->Middleway->Kearneysville; GEM's 39.4 km for P2040 = 24.48 mi, matching almost exactly -- see cross_row_leads). Also NOT the same asset as P0221 'Mountaineer XPress' (that is TC Energy/Columbia Gas Transmission's unrelated FERC interstate project -- correctly treated by this batch as a name collision, not a duplicate). IMPORTANT WIKI-CITATION HAZARD: gem.wiki's Mountaineer_Gas_Pipeline reference list conflates TWO causally-linked but legally and physically distinct projects: (a) Mountaineer Gas Co.'s own PSC-regulated EPME distribution line (this row, P0307/P2040), and (b) TC Energy/Columbia Gas Transmission's separate ~3.37-mile FERC-jurisdictional 'Eastern Panhandle Expansion Project' a.k.a. the 'Potomac Pipeline' (FERC Docket CP17-80), which crosses under the Potomac River near Hancock, MD to deliver NEW gas supply to Mountaineer's system at the Morgan County interconnection. Citations 7 (TC Energy fact sheet), 9-18 (Potomac River crossing opposition/litigation coverage: Post-Gazette, WTOP x3, Seeking Alpha, Chesapeake Climate Action Network, CBS Baltimore x2, GPO Federal Register CP17-80) all belong to the TC Energy transmission project, not to Mountaineer's own distribution Segment 1 -- I did not use them as support for this row's values and future researchers should not either. Of the 19 wiki-harvested citations, I opened/read 2 in full (Herald-Mail via Wayback; the rest of the detail came from an independent open-web search per the source ladder), verified 1 more resolves without full-reading (mountaineergasonline/about-us.html, a generic bio page), and could not extract content from 1 (oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/3288 -- a client-rendered SPA; both the live page and its 2023-03-30 Wayback snapshot returned an empty rendered shell with no embedded JSON, so I cannot confirm what it states). The remaining 15 wiki citations were read as belonging to the TC Energy transmission project (see above) and were not opened in full since standing rule scopes them out of this row.

As an intrastate LDC trunk line it is not FERC-jurisdictional and has no public FERC certificate stating added capacity; PSC filings that might contain a design-capacity figure are not available online in full text (Case No. 15-1256 exists only as a docket reference in secondary reporting, not as a directly fetchable PDF). Leaving blank rather than inferring from system-wide figures (Mountaineer serves ~220,000 accounts statewide -- an aggregate figure, not this segment's capacity).

One source (nuttalllegal.com, 2016, pre-segmentation project overview) describes the whole EPME project's operating pressure only qualitatively: 'about half the pressure of a typical transmission line, or several hundred PSI.' That is too vague and not segment-specific to stage as a numeric Pressure value for Phase I; no other source gives a number. Leaving blank rather than fabricating a PSI figure.
